title: Mounting Drosophila pupae for laser ablation and live imaging
author: O’Connor, Shannon, et al.
materials: Continuum Minilite II Q-switched Nd:Yag Laser

steps.title: Prepare genotype flies
steps.instruction: Maintain flies of genotype ActinP‑GCaMP6m / +; pnr‑Gal4, UAS‑mCherry.NLS, TubP‑Gal80TS / + at 29 °C for 4–5 days to inactivate Gal80TS and activate UAS‑mediated expression; note that development proceeds ≈1.3 × faster at this temperature.

steps.title: Set up laser ablation system
steps.instruction: Install a 3rd‑harmonic Q‑switched Nd:YAG laser (355 nm wavelength, 3 ns pulsewidth) or equivalent UV pulsed laser; route the beam through crossed polarizers, a coverslip beam‑splitter to an energy meter, a mechanical shutter, a pair of converging lenses (beam expander), and steering mirrors mounted on a rail; couple the beam into the microscope port (e.g., Zeiss Axiovert 135/LSM‑410 bottom port with extra converging lens, or Nikon Eclipse Ti2 back epi‑illumination port); include an appropriate UV‑transmitting dichroic and a UV‑compatible objective such as 40×/1.30 Plan‑Neofluor (Zeiss) or 40×/1.30 NA S Fluor (Nikon).

steps.title: Align laser to microscope
steps.instruction: Adjust the flat steering mirrors so the beam enters the chosen microscope port centrally and exits a blank turret position; insert a white business card or paper to visualize the near‑UV beam; close the shutter, rotate the turret to the imaging objective, place a fluorescein‑stained agarose slide as target, briefly open/close the shutter to ablate a spot, move the stage to fresh regions, rotate the crossed polarizers until ablations are ~1 µm in diameter, then fine‑tune the steering mirrors so the mark stays centered in the field of view.

steps.title: Adjust laser focus (z‑alignment)
steps.instruction: Switch the laser to single‑shot mode, open the shutter, deliver single pulses to fresh areas of the target while lowering pulse energy until the ablation mark is just barely visible; slightly change the separation between the two beam‑expander lenses and repeat; select the lens separation that yields the strongest marks as the optimal z‑alignment; re‑check x‑, y‑, and z‑alignment periodically.

steps.title: Stage pupae – method one
steps.instruction: Timing: 1–6 h before dissection. Under a dissection scope, classify each pupa in a vial of mixed 3rd‑instar larvae and pupae as (a) white prepupae (0–1 h APF, mark vial with “/”), (b) brown prepupae (1–12 h APF, mark with “X”), or (c) head‑everted pupae (≥12 h APF, mark with “•”). Return the vial to 29 °C and record the marking time. Within ≤6 h, re‑evaluate brown prepupae marked “X”; if they have become head‑everted, they are now 12–18 h APF and suitable for experiment. For tighter windows (e.g., 12–15 h APF) re‑evaluate after ≤3 h. Repeat steps 1–3 with a different colored marker for any remaining prepupae.

steps.title: Stage pupae – method two
steps.instruction: Timing: 12–17 h before dissection. Under a dissection scope, identify, classify, and mark every pupariated animal (prepupae and pupae) in the vial using the same symbols as method one, ensuring no animal is missed. Return the vial to 29 °C and note the time. ≤17 h later, re‑evaluate: white prepupae now head‑everted are 13–18 h APF; any previously unmarked larvae now head‑everted are 12–17 h APF. Both categories are appropriate for experimentation.

steps.title: Stage pupae – method three
steps.instruction: Timing: 12–17 h before dissection. Under a dissection scope, mark all white prepupae observed on the sides of several vials or bottles. Return the containers to 29 °C and record the marking time. After 12–17 h, all marked animals will be 12–18 h APF and ready for use (note this method requires ≈6 × more animals than the previous methods).
